newsitem.title: UK: Minor metals languish, seen picking up soon.
newsitem.headline: Minor metals languish, seen picking up soon.

text.p: The minor industrial metals failed to move significantly during the past week amid a general lack of interest following the Christmas and New Year holidays.
Traders said they expected conditions to pick up over the coming weeks on the back of consumer buying.
"If anything prices across the board look poised to head higher as consumers cover the first quarter requirements," one London trader commented.
All metals held near pre-Christmas levels, although titanium sponge and cadmium were showing signs of building on recent gains.
Demand from the aerospace industry and increased offtake by golf club manufacturers helped to underpin titanium.
Several traders believed prices would advance near-term.
"Sponge has the potential to climb above $10 a kilo by the second half of 1997," one trader said.
Long term contract negotiations, Japanese demand and speculative buying bolstered cadmium, while cobalt held steady also against a backdrop of demand from the aerospace industry.
Both indium and iridium sustained recent increases, but conditions remained slow, traders said.
